note: Supersedes an earlier application for the same period. Must be classed before the plain application rule or it is read as an original, and the period is then counted twice.

A MOTION FOR ENTRY OF AN ORDER IS NOT AN ORDER. Found on 2026-09-09: "Debtors' Motion for Entry of an Order Establishing Procedures for Interim Compensation" was classed as an order by the granting/approving rule below and its PDF was stored and then failed to parse, because a motion about compensation procedures contains no award and no timekeeper table. Ranked above every order rule so the word order inside a motion caption cannot claim it.
The court's own award. THIS IS THE ANSWER KEY for stage 5: it is written by a different author than the application it responds to.
Procedural. Carries no hours and no fees.
A notice of an application is not the application. Its text is a service list.
Proof that a document was served. Frequently the top hit for a fee-application query and never the document wanted.
An objection to someone else's fees. Relevant to a later build; not a source of the applicant's own hours.
A third party's review. Its numbers are derived from the applications rather than filed by the professional, so using it as a source would double-count.
Interim billing under a compensation order. Its periods are subsumed by the interim application that follows, so counting both double-counts the same hours.
Covers the whole case and re-presents every interim period. Never summed with the interims it supersedes.
The generic form. Lowest priority of the application rules so a more specific class wins first.
Last resort. Anything reaching here is an application of unstated period, and parse_status records that.
